items.title: The viewer's table of contents is now a real macOS sidebar
items.text: The selected heading uses the system's own selection colors and switches between them the way native sidebars do: an accent-filled pill with white text while the window is focused, neutral gray when it isn't. Rows no longer shift as you scroll past them.

items.title: Resize the contents card
items.text: Drag its right edge and the card, the gutter, and the document's text column all move together. Your width is remembered across panes and sessions.

items.title: Clicking a heading takes you there and stays there
items.text: Previously the highlight walked off the heading you clicked as the page smooth-scrolled past other sections. Now your click pins the selection until your next scroll gesture.

items.title: A pinned "CONTENTS" header on Liquid Glass
items.text: Headings scroll underneath it, and long tables of contents now show a scroll indicator so you can tell there's more below.

items.title: Glass cards line up
items.text: Every glass card (the contents sidebar, a pane banner in the pane next door) now leaves the same 12pt margin on all four sides, so their corners align and document text starts exactly one margin from the card.
